strings.name: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar
strings.summary: Born Lew Alcindor and raised in New York, Abdul-Jabbar won three college titles at UCLA and played 20 NBA seasons with Milwaukee and the Lakers. Known for the skyhook, he won six MVP awards and six championships and held the regular-season scoring record from 1984 to 2023. After retirement he wrote on Black history, racial equality and public culture.
strings.influence.rationale: NBA champion and long-time scoring record holder who also continues participating in public cultural discussion.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Six MVPs and six championships
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won six regular-season MVPs and six team championships across 20 NBA seasons.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Writing beyond basketball
strings.highlights.h2.text: Contributes to racial equality and cultural debates through histories, memoirs and commentary.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Presidential Medal of Freedom
strings.timeline.t1.text: Received the White House honour recognising sport and civic contributions.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Basketball Hall of Fame
strings.timeline.t2.text: Enshrined in the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame.
strings.timeline.t3.title: NBA retirement
strings.timeline.t3.text: Retired after 20 seasons, continuing writing and public activities.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Broke career scoring record
strings.timeline.t4.text: Passed Chamberlain’s regular-season total; his record stood until 2023.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Joined the Lakers
strings.timeline.t5.text: Moved from Milwaukee to Los Angeles, later winning five titles with the Lakers.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Bucks title and new name
strings.timeline.t6.text: Helped the Bucks win the title and publicly adopted Kareem Abdul-Jabbar that year.
strings.timeline.t7.title: College titles and NBA draft
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed UCLA’s three-title run and history degree, becoming the NBA’s first draft pick.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born in New York
strings.timeline.t8.text: Born Ferdinand Lewis Alcindor; later attended school in New York.
